open_points.subject: AuditEntry sequence allocator
open_points.text: “never reused, also after old entries are erased (R0-66) or the store is restored (State 2 A15)”
open_points.question: What durable fact or authority remembers the greatest sequence number ever minted when entries have been erased or the store is restored from a backup that predates later minting, and which model owns that fact?
options: A per-instance high-water mark outside the restored store
A high-water mark restored with the store plus a rule forbidding restoration of any backup older than the latest mint
Derive the next number from retained AuditEntries, which does not satisfy the stated guarantee after erasure or rollback
open_points.default_guess: Use a per-instance non-rollback high-water mark outside the restored store.

open_points.subject: Failed change sequence reservation
open_points.text: “A number minted for a change that did not commit is not used again” versus “a stale one is refused and nothing changes. Every change is atomic.”
open_points.question: Is advancing the audit sequence allocator an explicit exception to the guarantees that a refused or uncommitted change changes nothing and that every change is atomic, and exactly which failed attempts may advance it?
options: Any attempt that reserves a number advances durable allocator state even if its domain change does not commit
Only an accepted change that later fails during commit may burn a number; validation refusals mint none
Sequence allocation is transactional and aborted changes reuse the number, contradicting the new sentence
open_points.default_guess: Validation refusals mint nothing, but a number reserved for an accepted change may be burned if its commit later fails; the allocator advance is an explicit atomicity exception.

open_points.subject: MigrationClosure before a checked backup exists
open_points.text: “absent, then present forever: once a backup holding it has passed its check, no backup without it is kept”
open_points.question: Between successful import and the first checked backup containing the MigrationClosure, may an older backup without the closure be restored, and if not, what fact or lifecycle rule prevents that restoration and a second import?
options: The import is not successful and the closure is not considered permanent until such a backup passes its check
Import succeeds immediately, but every pre-closure backup becomes ineligible for restore at that moment
An external durable migration-completed marker survives restoration of an older backup
Older backups remain restorable during the interval, allowing the closure to disappear and the import to reopen
open_points.default_guess: Import succeeds immediately and all backups predating the closure become ineligible for restoration at that same point; they may be discarded after a checked replacement exists.
